stories.title_en: Paying Silver to Get the Woman Drying Paper

paragraphs.zh: 宗化人羽崇，家资殷富，性最好淫，常以银穀生放于乡下。乡人唯早午晚在家食饭，午前后都往耕田，并无男子在家。崇偏于半午前往人家取帐，遇单居妇女，千方挑之，多与通好。
paragraphs.en: Yu Chong of Zonghua was rich and lecherous. He often lent silver and grain in the countryside. Villagers were home only at morning, noon, and evening meals; the rest of the day they were in the fields, with no men in the house. Chong made a point of going to collect debts in mid-morning. When he found a woman alone, he tried every way to tease her, and he often got his way.

paragraphs.zh: 人有问之者曰：“凡妇人与初相见，面生情疏，茫不相识，怎好开口便通野话？倘怒骂起来，后何以登其门？”崇曰：“凡撩妇人，临机应变，因事乘机。或以言挑，或以利诱，或以势压，或以恳求，何止一端，全在察其心情而投中之。或无可入机者，试与之讲梦，说我昨夜梦一所在去，宛似你家一般，某物在此，某物在此。又梦与你相交，一夜快活，醒来乃是一梦。今日到此，全与梦中相同。如此且笑且说，讲了一遍，看她言貌或喜或怒，或不睬，或应对，或疑猜，便可以言投入。彼若发骂，我只说梦；彼若不拒，我便可取事矣。“我尝往一所在取帐。男子另一处造纸，两妯娌对焙纸。其伯姆半宿妇人，其婶子极是少美，我欲挑之。若半声推拒，隔焙便闻，何以动手？我生一计，包银一钱，作一块，密密轻轻与说曰：‘我欲挑你伯姆，把此一钱银送你；再一包五分，託你代送与伯姆，替我说个方便’。妇人接四包银，把自己包开看过，见银作一块，心中有些喜意，答曰：‘你爱她你自与她说，自然是替，我不好替说。’我便曰：‘若爱只是爱你，但恐你不肯，故託你通伯姆。’罢不应，我便搂之，默然应承。只隔焙幹事，那边全不知。若不如此，反生计较。彼恐伯姆知之，怎肯默然应允？惟先说挑伯姆，彼心道：‘那边可干事，我这边密密幹，亦何妨？’故不劳而成也。”
paragraphs.en: Someone asked him: “When you first meet a woman, you are strangers, with no feeling between you. How can you open your mouth with loose talk? If she flies into a rage and scolds you, how will you ever enter her door again?” Chong said: “Teasing a woman depends on reading the moment and using whatever is at hand. You may bait her with words, tempt her with profit, press her with status, or plead—there is more than one way. The whole art is to watch her mood and hit it. If there is no opening, try telling a dream: say that last night you dreamed you went to a place that looked just like her house, this thing here, that thing there; and you dreamed you were with her all night, then woke and found it was a dream; and today you arrive, and it is exactly as in the dream. Say this with a smile. Watch whether her face is pleased or angry, whether she ignores you, answers, or grows suspicious—then you know how to speak. If she scolds, I say it was only a dream. If she does not refuse, I can proceed. I once went to collect a debt. The men were making paper elsewhere; two sisters-in-law were drying paper facing each other. The elder brother’s wife was a woman of middle years; the younger brother’s wife was very young and pretty. I wanted to tease the younger one. If she made even half a sound of refusal, it would be heard across the drying rack—how could I act? I thought of a plan. I wrapped one qian of silver in a lump and said quietly: ‘I want to tease your sister-in-law. I’ll give you this one qian; here is another packet of five fen—please pass it to her and put in a word for me.’ The woman took four packets of silver, opened her own packet, saw the silver in a lump, and was somewhat pleased. She answered: ‘If you like her, tell her yourself. Of course I’ll help, but I shouldn’t be the one to speak.’ I said: ‘If I like anyone, I like you. I only feared you would refuse, so I asked you to speak to your sister-in-law.’ She did not answer. I embraced her, and she silently consented. We did it with only the drying rack between us; the other side never knew. If I had not done it this way, she would have calculated. She would have feared her sister-in-law would know, and would never have silently agreed. Only by first saying I wanted the sister-in-law would she think: ‘If that side can do it, I can do it quietly here too—what’s the harm?’ So it was done without effort.”

paragraphs.zh: 按：妇人不爱淫者亦爱财，但深畏人知，故不敢为。唯点壮其心，谓人不能知，彼便敢妄为耳。既许从你，彼之遮盖，自然更谨密矣。此羽崇骗姦机巧之一节也。然世情鬼魅，有许多深奸隐慝，何能尽述为戒？特择其近闻者如此。
paragraphs.en: Note: Women who do not love lust still love money, but they deeply fear being found out, so they dare not act. Only when you stiffen their courage by saying no one can know will they dare to go wrong. Once they have agreed to you, they will cover themselves even more carefully. This is one of Yu Chong’s tricks for illicit sex. But worldly wickedness has many deep, hidden schemes—how can they all be told as warnings? I only pick what I have recently heard.

stories.title_en: A Monk Cuts Silk to Seduce a Tenant’s Wife

paragraphs.zh: 寿山寺，田粮五百石，分为十二房。僧皆富足，都锦衣肉食，饮酒宿娼，更甚俗家。每管寺十餘年，银多欲归，先约家中定姻，在外蓄发为头陀，鬓发可缚网巾，即回娶妻当家矣。每兄去弟来，父亡子继，据为己业，并无异色人得参入。或有畏受家累，不思归俗者，辄择村中愚善佃客有无妻者，出银与代娶。僧先宿一个月，后付与佃客，供不时往宿，僧来则僧之妻，僧去则佃之妇。故谚云：“非僧奸佃妇，乃佃奸僧老婆。”即此俗也。或生子，有全月可认者，则属某；或交错无可辨者，则僧与佃分，各得其一，待十餘岁，即领为侍者，实则亲子也。故僧家云：“灭灯传道，寄姓传宗。”即此也。
paragraphs.en: Shoushan Temple had a grain tax of five hundred shi, split among twelve monastic households. The monks were all well off: silk clothes, meat, drinking, and visits to prostitutes—worse than laypeople. After managing the temple for ten-odd years, when they had enough silver and wanted to go home, they first arranged a marriage in the family, then grew their hair as itinerant monks. When the hair was long enough to bind with a hairnet, they went home, married, and kept house. Brothers succeeded brothers; sons succeeded fathers. They treated it as family property; no outsider could join. Some who feared family burdens and did not want to return to lay life would pick a simple, kind tenant in the village who had no wife, and pay silver to marry one for him. The monk slept with her first for a month, then handed her to the tenant, and came back to sleep with her whenever he liked: when the monk came she was the monk’s wife; when he left she was the tenant’s wife. Hence the saying: “It is not the monk who seduces the tenant’s wife—it is the tenant who sleeps with the monk’s woman.” That was the custom. If a child was born and the month made paternity clear, it belonged to that one; if mixed and unclear, monk and tenant split, each taking one. After about ten years they were taken as attendants—actually their own sons. Hence the monks said: “Put out the lamp to transmit the teaching; park the surname to continue the line.” That is this.

paragraphs.zh: 有一僧，往乡取苗租，其佃户柔懦。见其妇美貌，每挑之便骂，不睬。后冬十月，故买匹好绢，问此妇借剪刀，剪下二尺，曰：“将送人作鞋面。”餘者寄此妇手。两日后复来取绢，借剪刀又剪二尺，将往送人，餘者仍寄之。妇曰：“送甚人，何不全拿去？”僧曰：“只消许多，可长享用。”妇曰：“我代收藏，亦当剪二尺与我。”僧曰：“你若要，便全匹与你，这两尺亦与你，不消送那人矣。”妇曰：“果真乎？”僧曰：“惟恐你不受，我久有意送矣。”两下遂成云雨佳会。僧曰：“你往日骂我，今日何有这好意？”妇曰：“我冬间要做一身衣服，送母亲寿，故不得已从你。后日决不肯矣。”僧曰：“那二尺更要一次。”妇曰：“二尺任你送别人。”僧曰：“取多辞少，你好歹。”
paragraphs.en: One monk went to the village to collect seedling rent. The tenant was timid. Seeing that the wife was pretty, the monk teased her whenever he could; she always cursed and ignored him. Later, in the tenth month of winter, he deliberately bought a bolt of good silk, asked this woman to lend scissors, cut two chi, and said, “I’ll give this to someone for shoe uppers.” He left the rest in her hands. Two days later he came again for the silk, borrowed the scissors, cut another two chi to give someone, and left the rest with her again. The woman said, “Who are you giving it to? Why not take it all?” The monk said, “This much is enough; it will last a long time.” The woman said, “If I’m storing it for you, you should cut two chi for me too.” The monk said, “If you want it, I’ll give you the whole bolt, and these two chi as well—no need to give that other person.” The woman said, “Truly?” The monk said, “I only feared you wouldn’t take it; I’ve long meant to give it to you.” Then the two of them had sex. The monk said, “You used to curse me; why so kind today?” The woman said, “This winter I need a set of clothes to give my mother for her birthday, so I had no choice but to go along. After this I certainly will not.” The monk said, “Those two chi need one more time.” The woman said, “Give the two chi to someone else.” The monk said, “You take a lot and refuse a little—you’re a piece of work.”

paragraphs.zh: 及事完了出房，僧曰：“我要禾稿绞一索用。”妇取付之。僧将稿慢慢绞索。妇催快去，僧曰：“在外何妨？”少顷，佃客回，问曰：“你作索何用？”僧曰：“我有绢大半匹要卖，令正说要造衣，送令岳母寿，以你养的猪，作一两二钱还我绢，将此索牵去。”佃客骂妻曰：“我猪要养，何换此无用绢？急取还他去！”妇取起二尺，将大匹丢出还之，曰：“舍与你！”僧曰：“我还你是价，也不亏你，有甚舍与我？”僧见其取起二尺，知她终是爱财，次月复买蓝绢半匹，并前绢送与之。妇骂曰：“秃骡该入螺蛳地狱，我岂睬你！”僧曰：“正为你常骂我，故意取回，弄你受气。不然，我岂悭吝的？你说要一身衣服送寿，前日止一件衣，今敬剪一件下，成就你事，何故又骂？”妇拒不允，僧再三哀求，只前已有情了，终拒不得，复为受之。后遂通往来，难禁断矣。
paragraphs.en: When they were done and came out of the room, the monk said, “I need rice-straw to twist a rope.” The woman fetched some. The monk twisted the straw slowly. She urged him to leave quickly. The monk said, “What’s the harm of being outside?” Shortly the tenant returned and asked, “What’s the rope for?” The monk said, “I have most of a bolt of silk to sell. Your wife said she needs it to make clothes for your mother-in-law’s birthday, and would pay with a pig you raised, one tael two qian for the silk; this rope is to lead the pig away.” The tenant cursed his wife: “I need to raise that pig; why swap it for useless silk? Give it back at once!” The wife picked up the two chi, threw the large piece back, and said, “Take it as a gift!” The monk said, “I was paying you a fair price; I wasn’t cheating you. What’s this ‘gift’?” Seeing she had kept the two chi, he knew she still loved money. The next month he bought half a bolt of blue silk and brought it with the earlier silk. The wife cursed: “Bald mule, you belong in snail hell—you think I’ll pay you any mind?” The monk said, “Precisely because you always curse me, I deliberately took it back to make you angry. Otherwise would I be stingy? You said you needed a set of clothes for the birthday; last time it was only one garment. Now I respectfully cut another so you can finish the job—why curse again?” She refused. He pleaded again and again. Since they had already had relations, she could not hold out in the end, and accepted again. After that they kept meeting; it was hard to stop.

paragraphs.zh: 按：此妇性本烈，只为爱其绢，遂至玷身。所谓“枨也欲，焉得刚”是也。人家唯禁止僧道来往，便是好事。若入寺，若拜佛，若子寄僧道姓，此皆耻事，切宜戒之。勿图无影福田，而蹈无穷污垢也。
paragraphs.en: Note: This woman was originally fierce; only because she loved the silk did she stain herself. As the saying goes, “If one is full of desire, how can one be firm?” Households should simply forbid monks and Daoists from coming and going—that is already a good thing. Entering temples, worshipping Buddha, giving a child a monk’s or Daoist’s surname—these are all shameful; be sure to avoid them. Do not chase shadow-blessings in some unseen field of merit and step into endless filth.

stories.title_en: A Geomancer Leaves His Wife to Steal a Good Bloodline

paragraphs.zh: 有鲁地理，看山颇精。要图一好地，自葬父。寻至宁城，得一佳风水，落在杨乡官坟祠后，既难明买，又难盗葬。闻杨乡官已故，两公子亦欲求地葬父。鲁地理即以此地献，引二公子来看，果好穴情山。不费买，坐向又大利，即用葬父，将银三十两谢地理。鲁客不能谋其地，因欲脱其种。乃租杨公子花园门下住家，用银娶一美妇为妻，与居两个月，对妻曰：“我要出外行地理，难计归程。家下若欠缺薪米，已托主人公子看顾你。此是我恩人，因得他银，故能娶你。我已远出，这两公子若调戏你，随你从他。若与他有情，后日扶持你必厚。但他家多奴仆，切不可与他通。若轻自身，公子必看贱你，后自取困穷，谁来周济你？”又去托两公子：“见得要远出行，地理家下些少，望相周济，归时一一奉还。”
paragraphs.en: There was a geomancer named Lu, quite skilled at reading mountains. He wanted a fine gravesite to bury his own father. Searching as far as Ningcheng, he found excellent fengshui behind the ancestral shrine of Official Yang. It was hard to buy openly and hard to bury in secretly. He heard that Official Yang was already dead, and the two young masters also wanted a site to bury their father. Geomancer Lu offered them this site, led the two to look, and it was indeed a fine burial spot. No need to buy, and the orientation was very auspicious. They buried their father there and paid the geomancer thirty taels. Lu could not get the site himself, so he wanted to steal their seed. He rented a house at the garden gate of the Yang sons, used silver to marry a beautiful woman, lived with her two months, then told his wife: “I must go out to practice geomancy; I cannot say when I will return. If the household lacks firewood and rice, I have asked the young masters to look after you. They are my benefactors; because I got silver from them I could marry you. While I am far away, if these two young masters make advances, you may go along. If you have an affair with them, they will support you generously later. But they have many servants—never sleep with the servants. If you cheapen yourself, the young masters will look down on you, and you will end up poor with no one to help.” He also went and asked the two young masters: “I have to travel far; the geomancy household has little; please help out, and when I return I will repay everything.”

paragraphs.zh: 公子常往花园，见其妇美，已是动心。地理才去两日，大公子即来其家，调戏其妻。这妇人已承夫嘱，慨然与通，情意好甚。后月餘，次公子亦来戏之，亦从。半年后，鲁地理归，见家中米菜充足，问妻曰：“公子来否？”妻曰：“两人都来，我都纳之。”鲁地理曰：“与这好人交，亦不羞辱你。有吃有穿，有人陪你睡，早晚有人看顾，我虽出外亦安。”妻笑曰：“食用还强你在家时，只你不要吃醋。”地理曰：“是他银娶的，又代我供你，何须妒？但两人迭来，恐你惹毒疮。须与他定一月一个，可无生疮。”
paragraphs.en: The young masters often went to the garden, saw that the wife was beautiful, and were already stirred. Two days after the geomancer left, the elder came to the house and made advances. The woman, already instructed by her husband, readily consented, and they were very fond. After a month or so, the younger also came and teased her; she consented too. Half a year later Geomancer Lu returned, saw rice and vegetables plentiful, and asked his wife: “Did the young masters come?” The wife said: “Both came; I took them both.” Lu said: “To be with such good men is no shame to you. You have food and clothes, someone to sleep with, people looking after you morning and evening; I can rest easy even when away.” The wife laughed: “The food is even better than when you were home—just don’t get jealous.” The geomancer said: “It was their silver that married you, and they supply you in my place—why be jealous? But if both come in turn, you might catch sores. Set it as one month each, and you won’t get sores.”

paragraphs.zh: 再次又出外，公子又来。妇人曰：“你两位不时来，恐我成毒疮。须定单月大公子，双月小公子方好。”公子曰：“你说极是。自今某月属某，菜米一应他供给。”不觉经四年，已生两男子，皆两公子血脉矣。鲁地理将命与人推，皆云后当大富贵。因携妻与子辞两公子而归，二人各赠有厚程。后二子长成，皆登科第，实杨姓之风水，被其暗漏去而不知也。
paragraphs.en: He went out again; the young masters came again. The woman said: “You two come at odd times; I might get sores. Better: odd months the elder, even months the younger.” The young masters said: “You’re quite right. From now on such-and-such month belongs to such-and-such, and vegetables and rice are all supplied by that one.” Unnoticed, four years passed; two boys were born, both the young masters’ blood. Geomancer Lu had their fortunes told; all said they would later be very rich and noble. He took wife and sons, took leave of the two young masters, who each gave generous travel gifts. Later the two sons grew up and both passed the examinations—truly Yang’s fengshui, leaked away in secret without their knowing.

paragraphs.zh: 按：富贵家子弟，多有好淫人妻小者。或致生子，其风水不无分去。观此地理之脱种，后人可鉴矣。
paragraphs.en: Note: Sons of rich families often lust after other men’s wives. If children result, their fengshui is inevitably split away. Look at this geomancer stealing the seed—later generations can take warning.

paragraphs.zh: 有一富家子，往佃户家取租，见其妇美，累挑之。妇不敢从，密报于婆。婆曰：“他富家子，若与他有子，后日亦讨得吃。”富子后又挑之，妇即允，与入房中解衣。富子曰：“往时累说不从，今何故便肯？”妇曰：“已对婆婆说过了。”富子曰：“你婆要拿奸么？”妇曰：“非也！婆曰傍你富家种，若有儿，亦讨得吃。”富子一闻漏种话，猛然自省曰：“不可！不可！”连说四句“不可”，因转言曰：“我非真欲奸，只爱你生得好，故与耍耳。今送银三钱，与你买粉，我不污你也。”淫情已动，驰归家，夜与妻交。其夜受胎，后生一男，长中进士，官受知县。
paragraphs.en: A rich family’s son went to a tenant’s house to collect rent, saw that the wife was pretty, and propositioned her again and again. She dared not consent, and secretly told her mother-in-law. The mother-in-law said: “He’s a rich man’s son; if you have a child by him, later we’ll have something to eat.” The rich son propositioned her again; the woman agreed, and they went into the room to undress. The rich son said: “Before you always refused; why agree now?” The woman said: “I’ve already told Mother-in-law.” He said: “Does she want to catch us in the act?” The woman said: “No. She said to lean on your rich-family seed; if there’s a son, we’ll have something to eat.” At the words about leaking the seed, he suddenly woke: “No! No!” He said “No” four times, then changed his words: “I didn’t really mean to; I only liked your looks, so I was playing. Here’s three qian of silver for powder; I won’t stain you.” Lust already aroused, he hurried home and slept with his wife that night. She conceived that night; later a boy was born, grew up, passed as a jinshi, and became a county magistrate.

paragraphs.zh: 初上任日，天晴日朗，忽见官堂四大柱上，各有两个“不可”金字，心中忧曰：“此必不可任此官也。”谨慎做一季官，便推病辞官养亲，匆然归。父惊问故，答曰：“因上任日，见四个‘不可’金字，恐非吉光，故辞官归养。”父曰：“养亲官在亦可。”经一夜，父思到大喜，呼其子曰：“你见四‘不可’金字，此大吉兆，你官必高也。我少年时，挑一佃妇，已允矣。临行事时，他说要傍我好种，我猛省起，连说四句‘不可’，遂不肯苟合。其夜归后即生汝，此天报我不淫人妇之德。若是凶兆，何故是金字？又何故四个‘不可’，与我昔言相应也？此是好兆矣。”儿曰：“是也。”随即写书托同年，次年复起官。后官至侍郎，一门贵盛。
paragraphs.en: On the first day of taking office, the sky was clear. Suddenly he saw on the four great pillars of the hall two golden characters, “Must not,” on each. He worried: “I must not take this post.” He served carefully for one season, then claimed illness, resigned to care for his parents, and hurried home. His father asked in alarm. He answered: “On the day I took office I saw four golden ‘Must not’; I feared it was not auspicious, so I resigned to care for you.” The father said: “You can care for parents while in office too.” After a night, the father thought it over and was overjoyed. He called his son: “Those four golden ‘Must not’ are a great auspicious sign; your office will be high. When I was young I propositioned a tenant’s wife; she had already agreed. At the moment of the act she said she wanted to lean on my good seed. I suddenly woke and said ‘Must not’ four times, and would not go through with it. That night after I returned, you were conceived. This is Heaven rewarding me for not defiling another man’s wife. If it were an ill omen, why golden characters? Why four ‘Must not,’ matching what I once said? This is a good sign.” The son said: “Yes.” He immediately wrote to a classmate; the next year he was reinstated. Later he rose to Vice Minister; the whole family flourished.

paragraphs.zh: 看此节，可见富贵家子弟不可漏种于人矣。有乡官知县，生四男，皆为秀才，聪明俊伟。一日，乡官卒。地理为择一葬地，风水甚佳，曰：“六年两科内，四位公子当尽登科第。”六年后，地理来取谢。三长公子都中去为官，独四公子在家款待地理，敬问曰：“承先生许我四人皆发科，今三位兄果中矣。论才学，我更高于兄，独不中，何故？”明日，地理同四公子再登坟细看，曰：“论此地，虽几兄弟皆当中，其间不中者，必有故。”公子恳问何故，地理曰：“令先尊几岁生你？”公子曰：“先父生我时年六十，后七十四岁卒，今又六年矣。”又问曰：“令堂当时几岁？”公子曰：“其时三十岁。”地理摇头曰：“我知之矣。”公子曰：“先生知何缘故？”地理曰：“休怪我说。公子必欲中，须问太夫人，你是何人血脉？”公子会其意，夜设盛席，慢慢劝母醉饮。至二更后，吩咐亲人并奴婢等各先睡。四下无人，公子跪曰：“儿有所禀，不敢言。不知母亲愿我中否？”母曰：“三哥子都中了，我愿你中极切。有甚好歹事，但说无妨。”公子曰：“地理说我不是爹爹亲血脉，故不中。必须知谁实生我，方可中。”母本爱幼子，静夜又无人，酒后又醉了，不觉吐言曰：“地理果高见。彼时你父已六十，衙中某门子后生标致，我实与他生你。”公子已得实，次日谋于地理。地理曰：“须到彼处谋门子骸骨来，附葬旁，来科即中矣。”公子依言，往取而葬之，次科果中。
paragraphs.en: Look at this: sons of rich families must not leak their seed to others. A retired official who had been a magistrate had four sons, all xiucai, clever and handsome. One day the official died. A geomancer chose a burial site of excellent fengshui and said: “Within six years and two examination cycles, all four young masters will pass.” Six years later the geomancer came for thanks. The three elder sons had all passed and become officials; only the fourth was home entertaining the geomancer. He respectfully asked: “You promised all four of us would pass. My three brothers have indeed. In talent I’m even above them; I alone haven’t passed—why?” The next day the geomancer and the fourth son climbed the grave and looked carefully. The geomancer said: “By this site, all the brothers should pass; if one hasn’t, there must be a reason.” The son pressed him. The geomancer asked: “How old was your late father when he had you?” The son said: “Father was sixty when I was born; he died at seventy-four; that’s another six years now.” He asked again: “How old was your mother then?” The son said: “Thirty.” The geomancer shook his head: “I know now.” The son said: “What do you know?” The geomancer said: “Don’t take offense. If you must pass, you must ask the old lady whose blood you are.” The son understood. That night he set a rich feast and slowly got his mother drunk. After the second watch he told relatives and servants to go to bed first. With no one around, he knelt: “I have something I dare not say. Does Mother want me to pass?” The mother said: “Your three brothers all passed; I want you to pass most of all. Whatever it is, good or bad, just say it.” The son said: “The geomancer says I’m not Father’s own blood, that’s why I don’t pass. I must know who really fathered me before I can pass.” The mother loved her youngest; it was a quiet night, no one else, and she was drunk—she let it out: “The geomancer sees truly. At that time your father was already sixty. A certain page in the yamen was young and handsome; I actually had you with him.” The son had the truth. The next day he consulted the geomancer. The geomancer said: “You must go there, get the page’s bones, and bury them beside the grave; next cycle you’ll pass.” The son did so, fetched and buried them; next cycle he indeed passed.

paragraphs.zh: 看此节，可见暗中杂种，人不及知，故有共风水而贵贱悬隔者，其中不无难言处也。
paragraphs.en: Look at this: mixed blood in secret, people don’t know; so some share the same fengshui yet are worlds apart in rank—there are always things hard to speak of.

paragraphs.zh: 又解某之父，血衰无子。其母夏月热甚，着单裙睡于床。家蓄有猴公，往奸之。惊醒欲推去，猴欲啮欲抓，推去不得。睡熟神旺，不觉淫情动，即有孕。解父归，妻与言被猴奸之故，曰：“此异物，须杀之。”猴既奸后心亏，走于后门大桃树上，不肯下。解父故与妻戏于树下。猴见人色喜，方下树来。解父槌杀之，即埋于桃树下。后解某生，极聪明伶俐，但跳跃倒地，若猴状。解母心知为猴种也。以无别子，故不杀之。八岁父死，地理为择葬曰：“此地极佳，当出神童才子。此子虽不才，但三年后可登高第。”过三年后，地理复来。解母曰：“汝说三年后此子知变，今轻狂如前，奈何？”地理再往坟细看，归问曰：“此子是安人亲生的，抑妾生乎？”解母曰：“此子非亲生，是邻家丫头与猴生的，欲弃之，我以无子，故血抱以养。”地理曰：“欲此子成器，须得猴骨在，附葬此冢之旁，后日还昌你家。”解母往树下掘之，其骨犹在。特与地理曰：“邻人尚留骨在，当如何处？”地理教择吉日葬之。再三年，果举神童，后为一代名人。（此闻其乡陈地理所传。）
paragraphs.en: Also: Xie So-and-so’s father had weak blood and no son. In the summer heat his mother slept on the bed in a thin skirt. The household kept a male monkey; it came and raped her. She woke and tried to push it off; the monkey would bite and claw, and she could not push it away. When she fell back asleep, vitality stirred; lust arose without her noticing, and she conceived. When Xie’s father returned, his wife told him of the monkey rape and said: “This is a freak; it must be killed.” After the rape the monkey felt guilty, went to a big peach tree at the back gate, and would not come down. Xie’s father pretended to sport with his wife under the tree. The monkey saw the sex, was pleased, and came down. The father clubbed it to death and buried it under the peach tree. Later Xie So-and-so was born, extremely clever, but he leapt and tumbled like a monkey. The mother knew in her heart he was monkey-seed. Having no other son, she did not kill him. At eight his father died. A geomancer chose a burial and said: “This site is excellent; it will produce a child prodigy and talent. This boy isn’t much now, but in three years he can rise to high rank.” After three years the geomancer returned. Mother Xie said: “You said after three years this boy would change; he’s still as wild as before—what now?” The geomancer went back to the grave, looked carefully, returned, and asked: “Is this boy your own, or a concubine’s?” Mother Xie said: “He’s not my own; a neighbor’s maid had him by a monkey; they wanted to abandon him; I had no son, so I took him to nurse.” The geomancer said: “If you want this boy to amount to something, you need the monkey’s bones buried beside this grave; later it will still prosper your house.” Mother Xie went under the tree and dug; the bones were still there. She told the geomancer: “The neighbors still have the bones; what should we do?” The geomancer told her to pick an auspicious day to bury them. After another three years he was indeed recommended as a child prodigy, later a famous man of his generation. (This was heard from Geomancer Chen of that district.)

paragraphs.zh: 看此节，可见风水之效，捷如影响。人家得好地者，子孙宜守礼法，不可淫欲败德，致漏脉于人也。
paragraphs.en: Look at this: the effect of fengshui is as swift as shadow and echo. Families that get a good site should have descendants keep rites and law, not ruin virtue with lust and leak the bloodline to others.

stories.title_en: An Affair with Someone’s Maid, Then the Silver Is Stolen

paragraphs.zh: 宁城一人，姓李名英，年二十餘岁，聪明脱洒，惟耽酒色。常买夏布，往苏州阊门外，寓牙人陈四店。其店兼卖白酒。邻家林廷节，常遣婢京季来买酒。季年方十八，国色娇媚。李英爱之，因而调戏成奸，买簪圈等送之。同店多有谏其勿惹祸者。英与季两少相爱，情深意美，哪肯割断？后廷节察知季与英有奸，呼季责曰：“你与李客私通，我姑恕汝。可密窥英银藏于何处，偷来置些衣装与你，后得享用。”
paragraphs.en: In Ningcheng there was a man named Li Ying, a little over twenty, clever and free-and-easy, only addicted to wine and women. He often bought summer cloth, went outside Chang Gate in Suzhou, and lodged at broker Chen Si’s shop. The shop also sold white liquor. Neighbor Lin Tingjie often sent the maid Jing Ji to buy wine. Ji was just eighteen, a rare beauty. Li Ying liked her, teased her into an affair, and bought hairpins and bangles for her. Others in the shop often warned him not to court disaster. Ying and Ji were young and in love, with deep feeling—who would cut it off? Later Tingjie found out that Ji and Ying were having an affair. He called Ji and scolded her: “You’ve been privately with Guest Li; I’ll pardon you this once. Secretly watch where Ying hides his silver, steal it, and I’ll buy you some clothes to enjoy later.”

paragraphs.zh: 一日，英饮酒娼家。季潜开英房，盗去银一百餘两。及英回店，知银有失，向店主逼取。客伙吴伦曰：“你房内有银，不可远饮娼家；即饮亦宜早归。今荡饮致失，何干主人事？今午见京季入你房中，必此女偷去。你可告于官，我与店主为证。”
paragraphs.en: One day Ying was drinking at a brothel. Ji quietly opened Ying’s room and stole over a hundred taels. When Ying returned to the shop and found the silver gone, he pressed the shop owner to make good. Fellow guest Wu Lun said: “If you have silver in your room, you shouldn’t drink far off at brothels; even if you drink you should come back early. You drank wildly and lost it—what’s it to the owner? This noon I saw Jing Ji go into your room; it must be this girl who stole it. You can report it to the officials; I’ll witness with the shop owner.”

paragraphs.zh: 英待两日，季不来店，乃告于府。廷节诉英欺奸伊婢，情露惧告，先以失银诬抵。本府张爷审问于证，吴伦、陈四证曰：“亲见季入英房，盗去银是实。”张爷诘曰：“客人房、室女床，二者岂容妄入？季入英房，汝等见何不阻？”伦曰：“英与季私通，亦是实，故英未在店，开门而盗。”张爷审出此情，知银系季偷是的；奈廷节乃府庠生，季考取之第二，只依廷节所诉，断曰：“既有奸情，则失银系是抵饰。以英不合欺奸侍婢，虚词抵赖。陈四为牙，知有奸情，何不谏英早改？待事败而犹偏证，各拟杖惩。”
paragraphs.en: Ying waited two days; Ji did not come to the shop. He sued at the prefecture. Tingjie claimed Ying had seduced his maid; the affair exposed, fearing a lawsuit, Ying had first used the lost silver as a false countercharge. Prefect Zhang questioned the witnesses. Wu Lun and Chen Si testified: “We personally saw Ji enter Ying’s room and steal the silver.” Prefect Zhang pressed: “A guest’s room and a maiden’s bed—neither should be entered lightly. If you saw Ji enter Ying’s room, why didn’t you stop her?” Lun said: “Ying and Ji having an affair is also true; so when Ying wasn’t in the shop, she opened the door and stole.” Prefect Zhang found this out and knew the silver was indeed stolen by Ji; but Tingjie was a prefectural-school student, ranked second in the last exam, so he followed Tingjie’s complaint and ruled: “Since there was an illicit affair, the lost silver is a covering excuse. Li Ying was wrong to seduce a serving maid and then lie. Chen Si as broker knew of the affair; why didn’t he advise Ying to stop sooner? After it blew up he still testified one-sidedly. Each is sentenced to beating.”

paragraphs.zh: 按：此审李英甚枉。特为客旅，宜谨慎自持，岂有奸人侍婢而不取祸者！今店中多有以妻女引诱客人，成奸后赖其财本者。切宜识透此套，勿入其骗可也。
paragraphs.en: Note: This judgment was very unjust to Li Ying. Especially as a traveling merchant, one should be careful and self-restrained; who has an affair with someone’s maid and does not bring disaster? Nowadays many shops use wives and daughters to lure guests; after the affair they cheat them of their capital. See through this trick; do not fall into it.

stories.title_en: An Affair with a Broker’s Daughter, Then the Swindle

paragraphs.zh: 经纪廖三号龙潭者，有女名淑姬，年方二八，尚未配人。容如月姊，貌赛花仙，真个女子中班头，绝世无双者。客人张鲁，年二十餘岁，磊落俊雅，颇谙诗书，浪迹江湖。一日，买闽笋数十担，在廖三店中发卖。不时遇风，都放帐未收。日久，见其女丰姿娇媚，日夜想慕，不能安枕。奈廖三家中人众，难以动手。而女亦时于门后偷眼觑鲁。鲁以目挑之，女为俯首作娇羞态。二人情意已通，只阳臺路隔，鹊桥难渡矣。
paragraphs.en: Broker Liao San, style Longtan, had a daughter named Shuji, just sixteen, not yet betrothed. Her face was like the moon goddess, her looks rivaling a flower immortal—truly first among girls, unmatched in the world. Guest Zhang Lu, a little over twenty, handsome and elegant, somewhat learned in poetry and books, was wandering the rivers and lakes. One day he bought several dozen loads of Fujian bamboo shoots and sold them at Liao San’s shop. Because of frequent weather delays, all were on credit not yet collected. Over time, seeing the daughter’s charming looks, he longed day and night and could not sleep. But Liao San’s household was crowded, hard to act. The girl also sometimes peeked at Lu from behind the door. Lu teased with his eyes; she lowered her head in a shy pose. Their feelings had already connected; only the road between them was blocked, the magpie bridge hard to cross.

paragraphs.zh: 一日，廖三家中早起炊饭，与商人上乡讨帐。张鲁心喜，乘机潜入其房，与廖女成姦。偷情之后，时有私会。
paragraphs.en: One day Liao San’s household rose early to cook, and he went with merchants to the countryside to collect accounts. Zhang Lu was glad, slipped into her room, and they had sex. After that they sometimes met privately.

paragraphs.zh: 其母知之，与夫商议曰：“吾女几多豪门求婚，未肯轻许。今被鼠客所玷，须密捕杀之，以消其恨。”廖三曰：“不可。凡妻与人私通，当场捉获，併斩呈官，律方无罪。今女与人通姦，併杀则不忍；单杀客人，被罪不至死，岂死无后话？现今笋帐已完，其银皆在我手。密窥女与姦时，当场捉之，打他半死，以锁繫住，勒其供状，怕他不把笋银献我，彼时亦何说？”妻然之。
paragraphs.en: The mother found out and discussed it with her husband: “How many rich families have sought our daughter, and we wouldn’t lightly agree. Now she’s been stained by a rat of a guest. We should secretly catch and kill him to quench the hate.” Liao San said: “No. If a wife commits adultery, catching them in the act and killing both, then presenting them to officials, the law finds you not guilty. Now it’s a daughter in an affair: killing both I can’t bear; killing only the guest, her crime isn’t a capital one, so if he dies there will be later trouble. Right now the bamboo-shoot accounts are settled; the silver is all in my hands. Secretly watch when the girl is with him, catch them in the act, beat him half to death, lock him, force a confession—won’t he hand over the shoot silver? Then what can he say?” The wife agreed.

paragraphs.zh: 未数日，张鲁果堕其术。鲁曰：“此是我不良。银须以一半还我便罢，不然吾不甘心。”廖三不允，鲁遂告于府，批刑馆。吴爷审出实情，问淑姬：“曾许配人否？”对曰：“未配。”又问鲁：“曾娶否？”鲁已有发妻，乃诳曰：“发妻已死，尚未再娶。”吴爷断曰：“汝二人既未成婚，须断合之，以所勒银准作财礼。”廖三曰：“奸人室女而得成婚，后何以儆？”吴爷曰：“汝牙家常以妻女赖人姦而脱其银，吾岂不知？若不配合，须将汝女官卖，将银究论；张鲁合惩通姦之罪耳。”鲁曰：“一女子安值财礼一百餘两？须判一半还我，准与其女为奁。”吴爷曰：“为商而嫖花街柳巷，尚宜有节；主人室女，岂容欺姦？”鲁且感且哭，尽丧其本，止得一女，又无盘缠可带，即转嫁银三十两而归。
paragraphs.en: Within days Zhang Lu fell into the trap. Lu said: “This was my fault. Give me back half the silver and we’ll drop it; otherwise I won’t rest.” Liao San refused. Lu sued at the prefecture; it was sent to the criminal office. Judge Wu found out the truth and asked Shuji: “Have you been betrothed?” She said: “Not yet.” He asked Lu: “Are you married?” Lu already had a wife, but lied: “My first wife is dead; I haven’t remarried.” Judge Wu ruled: “Since neither of you is married, they should be matched; the silver extorted will count as the bride-price.” Liao San said: “If a man who seduces a virgin then gets to marry her, how will later people be warned?” Judge Wu said: “You brokers often use wives and daughters to trap guests into affairs and strip their silver—do I not know? If they aren’t matched, I’ll have your daughter sold by the government and the silver investigated; Zhang Lu will still be punished for the affair.” Lu said: “How is one girl worth over a hundred taels of bride-price? Order half returned to me, counting as her dowry.” Judge Wu said: “A merchant who visits brothels should still have limits; how can he seduce the host’s virgin daughter?” Lu was both grateful and weeping; he lost all his capital, got only a girl, and had no travel money to take her, so he remarried her off for thirty taels and went home.

paragraphs.zh: 按：牙家纵容妻女与客人成姦，后脱其财本，此常套也。惜此女不知，为父母作货；张鲁亦不知，而落此套中。犹幸吴爷断与成婚，虽失利，犹得妇也。惜其财本稀少，不得同此女归耳。后之为商者，断合事本难期望，则脱姦宜慎防之。
paragraphs.en: Note: Brokers letting wives and daughters have affairs with guests, then stripping their capital—this is a common trick. Pity this girl did not know she was merchandise for her parents; Zhang Lu also did not know, and fell into the trap. Luckily Judge Wu ordered them married; though he lost the money, he still got a wife. Pity his capital was so thin he could not take the girl home. Later merchants: expecting a court-ordered marriage is hard; better guard carefully against being stripped through an affair.
